facts.text: Revenue from the Chitimacha casino helped restore land that had once been part of the reservation, bringing the community back to its historic roots.
The Chitimacha are a key part of Charenton's history and continue to shape its cultural identity.
Charenton’s small community blends tribal and non‑Native residents, reflecting the tribe’s enduring presence after historic land reductions.
The area faces environmental challenges, with hurricanes, flooding, and historic storm surges, and Louisiana’s coastal land loss once exceeded 16 square miles per year.
The Chitimacha people, whose name means “men altogether red” or “warrior,” once controlled vast territories including the Atchafalaya Basin and Bayou Teche.
Charenton’s waterfront setting and historic charm give a glimpse into traditional Louisiana bayou life.
